chapter: Growing up with music in Austin
title: Playing tuba with Sammy LaPalm's orchestra and meeting Herschel Evans
summary: He was hired by the Holmes brothers' LaPalm Orchestra where he met Herschel, and Dance asks about road-show musicians.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And while I was working with our group, the Moonlight Serenaders, we had Sammy LePalm's orchestra in. That was the Holmes Brothers. They had a band, and they'd hire me on their jobs when I wasn't busy with my own. And that's how I met Herschel. I couldn't play much --
: Well, wait a minute. Is this band -- you're playing what?
This is the E flat Helicon Filica.
: Oh, that's what you played in this band?
: And who was this band, where Herschel was that you played with?
That was the Sammy LePalm Orchestra. Sammy Holmes and his LaPalm Orchestra. Now, that was about five or six pieces. Two brothers played. I know Tommy played

sax, I don't remember if Sammy played sax or trombone. But Wooty Holmes was the vocalist and the director. It was always great to have a director in a band, you know. He'd be standing up there, you know (inaudible). And --
Was Herschel playing tenor then, or --

Herschel came in and played tenor very shortly, you know. And Buddy Tate said he came in and played with that band, too. I might not have been on that particular gig that night. But I do remember Herschel.
Well, they were not professional musicians?

Well, in those days, let me tell you, it's like this. You might call them professionals. In those days there were lots of road shows. And it was -- although Herschel came from very near Austin, some little town that they say he didn't own when he died, somewhere like 28 miles from Austin. Now, he may not have been stranded, but there were many cases where musicians with some carnival or road show -- would hire them and get them out so far and drop them. Get up and leave in the middle of the night, and leave them here. And so you had lots of those.
I had several offers. One guy, Sir Jerome (PHONETIC) from Chicago --
